texts.facts: Sample of 1500 grams of Chhena Chap was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules, and were divided into three parts. 3. As per complaint, one sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 07.11.2005, the PA found the sample adulterated because it contains added vegetable oil which is not declared as one of the ingredients. It is noteworthy that PA had carried out the analysis from 21.10.2005 to 25.10.2005 as per the report. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by Tusli Ram Aggarwal vs . The State [Govt. on 2 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2765443/ 1 FI. Accordingly, sanction under Section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained and the complaint was filed on 20.03.2006 against the appellant for violation of Section 2(ia) (a) (b) (c) and (m) of PFA Act, punishable under Section 7/16 (1)(a) of PFA Act. 4. The appellant was summoned vide order dated 20.03.2006. An application under Section 13 (2) of the Act was filed by the appellant but the same was withdrawn on 18.04.2006. 5. Notice of accusation was served on the accused for violation of provisions of the Act punishable u/s 7/16 (1) (a) PFA Act read with Section 2(ia) (a) (b) (c) and (m) of PFA Act on 20.03.2009, to which he pleaded not guilty. 6. The prosecution examined 3 witnesses namely, PW1 FI Sh. P.C. Tiwari, PW2 FA Sh. Bhopal Singh and PW3 Sh. Anil Aggarwal. 7. The statement of the accused was recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. in which he claimed his innocence. 9. The present matter pertains to a period when there were no notified laboratories nor methods of analysis. 10. In the present case, the samples were examined by the Public Analyst from 21.10.2005 to 25.10.2005.
texts.arguments: For this it would be relevant to refer to the provisions of Section 23(1A)(ee) and (hh) which read as follows: "23(1A) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:- ............................ (ee) defining the laboratories where samples of articles of food or adulterants may be analysed by public analysts under this act; ....................... (hh) defining the methods of analysis." 15. The present Rule 4(9) reads as follows:- "The manuals of method of analysis brought out by Ministry of Health and Family Welfare shall be adopted for analysing the samples food articles. These aspects were considered by the Apex Court in the case of Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. vs. Food Inspector & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC (Cri) 8. 18. This judgment of the Apex Court was followed by the Kerala High Court in the case of R. Gopalakrishnan Vs. Food Inspector in Criminal Revision Petition No.671/2002 decided on 17.07.2013. Special Leave Petition against the said judgment was preferred in Supreme Court of India, vide Criminal Appeal No. 2476 of 2014, but the same was dismissed. Tusli Ram Aggarwal vs . The State [Govt. on 2 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2765443/ 3 19. In a recent judgment of M/s Nestle India Ltd. Vs. the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and Ors. 2015 (2) FAC 56 the Bombay High Court has again followed the Pepsico case (supra) to observe that in the absence of designated laboratories and validated methods of analysis, the reports of the Public Analyst and the Director, CFL, cannot be relied upon. 20. Reliance is also placed upon the decision of the Hon'ble Kerala High Court in Mohanan P. & Others Vs. State of Kerala and Another, Crl. Rev. P.No. 66 of 2011, decided on 25th November, 2021 where the earlier decision in R. Gopalakrishnan (supra) has again been followed. 23. In Dhian Singh Vs. Municipal Board Saharanpur, AIR 1970 SC 318, the Hon'ble Supreme Court was of the view that the report of the PA need not contain the mode or particular of analysis nor the test applied. The decision in Dhian Singh (Supra), most respectfully, would cease to be the applicable law on the aspect in view of the specific legislative mandate introduced by way of amendment.
